name: אינטגרל מסוים בחלקים פעמיים – x²·cos(x) (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Evaluate the following definite integral:

\( \displaystyle \int_{{CT:0}}^{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}}\,d{{CT:3}} = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Integrate by parts twice to find an antiderivative, then evaluate it at the limits.
Step 1 — First integration by parts
If

\[ \int f(x) dx = F(x) \]

then

\[ \int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b). \]

Using integration by parts,

\[ \int u dv = uv - \int v du, \]

by defining \(u = {{CT:4}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:5}} d{{CT:3}}\) so that \(du = {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}}\) and \(v = {{CT:7}}\). Then,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &= \int u dv \\ &= uv - \int v du \\ &= {{CT:4}}\cdot \left({{CT:7}}\right) - \int {{CT:7}}\cdot \left({{CT:6}}\right) d{{CT:3}} \end{aligned} \]

Step 2 — Second integration by parts
To calculate

\[ \int {{CT:8}}d{{CT:3}} \]

we will have to use parts again, by defining \(u = {{CT:6}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:7}}d{{CT:3}}\) so that \(du = {{CT:9}}d{{CT:3}}\) and \(v = {{CT:10}}\). So,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int {{CT:8}}d{{CT:3}} &= \int u dv \\ &= uv - \int v du \\ &= {{CT:6}}[{{CT:10}}] - \int [{{CT:10}}]{{CT:9}}d{{CT:3}} \\ &= {{CT:11}} - \int {{CT:12}}d{{CT:3}} \\ &= {{CT:13}} \end{aligned} \]

Step 3 — Combining and evaluating at the limits
Hence,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &= {{CT:14}} - ({{CT:13}}) \\ &= {{CT:15}} \\ &= {{CT:16}} \end{aligned} \]

Lastly, we evaluate this expression at the limits to give

\[ \left[{{CT:17}}\right]_{{CT:0}}^{{CT:1}} = {{CT:18}}. \]

on_true.feedback: This is a definite integration problem, so your answer should be a number. This is the correct integral, but you have not evaluated it.
